text: Labor has done little to educate the public on the benefits of cleaner fuels.
explanation: Criticism of Labor's public education efforts on cleaner fuels; instrumental/performance critique, no moral language.

text: In 1997, a single person on the average industrial wage paid 22% of their income in income tax.
explanation: Tax-burden statistic; purely empirical fiscal claim.

text: Together we're the co-leaders of the Green party
explanation: Descriptive statement of party leadership roles; no moral content.

explanation: Instrumental equality-of-access commitment (arts access for disadvantaged young people); the negative clarification codes instrumental access arguments and descriptive references to disadvantaged/vulnerable groups as 0 absent explicit moral vocabulary.

text: Direct this new spending to health, education, and a few carefully targeted initiatives.
explanation: A neutral description of spending allocation to policy areas; instrumental language with no moral vocabulary (negative clarification: neutral description of policy instruments/funding).

text: The Green Party is committed to bringing rail services into public ownership and control.

text: • Conflicting roles and responsibilities.
explanation: Administrative description of conflicting roles; no evaluative or moral content.

text: An SNP government will strive to ensure that Scotland becomes a world leader in securing a sustainable environment
explanation: An aspirational goal (world leader in sustainability) without moral vocabulary; falls under aspirational visions lacking moral-evaluative language.

text: With the investment that we are promising in hospital buildings,
explanation: A funding/investment promise for hospital buildings; instrumental with no moral language.

text: The question that should still be asked of Labor is:

text: And with new laws to crack down on domestic violence,
explanation: Domestic violence is a morally charged subject, but the text is a descriptive policy statement about new laws to 'crack down'; per the negative clarification, instrumental references to morally charged subjects without moral-evaluative language are coded 0.

text: Fine Gael will support the on-going nationwide roll out of the “Food Dudes” Fruit and Vegetable Promotion programme to all primary schools in Ireland.

text: We will give 1 weeks paid Parental leave for either parent to take, giving them more choice.
explanation: A parental leave entitlement framed as practical 'choice' for parents; not an appeal to freedom as a value being protected, so it remains instrumental policy.

text: Policy alignment will ensure the wise use of public dollars.
explanation: Fiscal efficiency argument ('wise use of public dollars'); economic/administrative framing, coded 0 per the negative clarification.

text: At £1.4 Trillion, that equates to £54,353 per household;

explanation: 'Proud reputation' is a generic positive descriptor of the Defence Forces' record; no explicit moral vocabulary, so treated as a generic positive adjective case.

explanation: Uses explicit moral vocabulary: a 'fair legal system' that 'respects the rights ... of all Australians' and eliminating a geographic 'divide'; matches clarification (a) on fair/rights language.

text: These moves will eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system and enhance its progressive nature.
explanation: Although technocratic in context (income tax), it explicitly invokes eliminating 'inequality'; clarification (a) lists equality/inequality as moral vocabulary, so coded 1.

text: It is now enshrined in law that we must pay 0.7 per cent of our Gross National Income (GNI) on aid every year.
explanation: A factual statement about a legal spending requirement on aid; 'must' here is legal compliance, not a moral imperative, and no moral vocabulary is used.

text: Caroline Lucas and housing In July 2014 Caroline Lucas MP introduced a Housing (Affordability, Supply and Tenant Protection) Bill to highlight the problems faced by private tenants.
explanation: Descriptive account of a bill being introduced; 'problems faced by private tenants' is descriptive, not moral-evaluative.

text: Support for 2,500 additional aged care beds;
explanation: A funding commitment for aged care beds; neutral policy instrument description.

text: Develop new community policing structures, through local policing forums in individual communities, to reconnect the Gardaí and local communities in a spirit of genuine partnership.
explanation: Community policing reform; 'spirit of genuine partnership' is aspirational phrasing without moral vocabulary from the codebook's list.

text: We will: save you money by cutting government waste
explanation: Cutting government waste to save money; an economic/efficiency argument coded 0 per the negative clarification.

text: Ireland should be the best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old.
explanation: An aspirational vision ('best place in the world to grow up and grow old') using generic superlatives without moral vocabulary.

text: Ministerial Cars: We will end the automatic entitlement to a State car for every Government Minister.
explanation: Administrative/political reform ending ministers' automatic state cars; 'entitlement' here describes a perk, not a moral claim about desert.

text: If you can’t trust Labour and National to go public about poisoned baby milk then what on earth can you trust them on.
explanation: A partisan attack about political trustworthiness on a specific disclosure issue; 'trust' here is a reliability jab rather than the virtue/moral vocabulary in the codebook, so treated as a partisan attack lacking moral-evaluative language.

text: All TDs will be entitled to put forward proposals for legislation and a lottery at the start of each session will determine which Bills will be debated.
explanation: Procedural reform for debating private members' bills; neutral institutional description.

text: We will put in train preparations for the 100th anniversary of the Easter Rising, in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week,
explanation: Primarily about preparations for a commemoration; 'honours the contribution' is standard ceremonial phrasing. Borderline (honouring national forebears has a patriotic tint), but the text itself is administrative event-planning without moral-evaluative claims.

text: We will support sensible immigration policies that meet our economic needs
explanation: Immigration policy justified by economic needs; instrumental/economic framing with no moral vocabulary.

text: Establishing the right accountability framework for schools.
explanation: School accountability framework; 'right' here means appropriate/correct, an administrative judgment, not a moral rights claim.

text: Republicans share President Bush's understanding that just as events in Europe determined the outcome of the Cold War, events in the broader Middle East will set the course for the victory of free nations in the War on Terror.
explanation: Invokes 'the victory of free nations' and 'the War on Terror'; the definition includes freedom as a value and 'terror' as vice language, matching clarification (b)/(c).

text: • there is appropriate time for debate to be conducted.

text: All recreational fishers should help police the system to ensure that there is no room for poachers and quasi ‘recreational’ fishers who sell or raffle their catches.

text: Half a million of us regularly play sport, while 400,000 volunteer as coaches, match officials and referees.

text: We recognise the contribution that Mäori enterprise and entrepreneurship has made to our nation's economy.
explanation: Recognises Māori enterprise's economic contribution; framed economically with no moral-evaluative vocabulary.

text: We will: Work to secure the full implementation of the Military Covenant in Northern Ireland.
explanation: A policy commitment to implement the Military Covenant; although the covenant concept implies obligation, the text itself is an implementation pledge with no moral vocabulary.

text: abolish the current 2% limit for funding political parties, which acts against new and smaller parties and could be seen as supporting the status quo;

text: Processing of applications and decision-making is subject to long delays, while the absence of legislation means there is frequent resort to the Courts for judicial review.
